publicReleaseNotes: Penny 0.1.4 fixes backup, restore and erasure on RER Managed. An installation that RER Managed (RER Platform) installs records its migrations in its own ledger table, rer_migrations, which Penny 0.1.3 and earlier did not recognise, so Data → Export, restoring a backup and erasing personal data all refused with unclassified_archive_schema: the owner could not back up, move or restore Penny. 0.1.4 treats that table as the installation's bookkeeping: it never goes into a backup and a restore never changes it, and on every backup and restore it must list exactly this version's migrations with their file hashes, else Penny refuses with migration_history_mismatch. Any other unknown table still refuses. 0.1.4 also ships everything on main since 0.1.2: custom internal statuses and the public status roadmap, categories and board controls, decline and blocking controls, opt-in vote subscriptions, workspace timezone and quiet hours, private ownership and My queue, internal replies and mentions, triage ageing and reminders, public roadmap ETAs, merge notices, reviewed Canny imports of board settings, statuses and roadmaps, native proxy votes and vote importance, a product hierarchy, saved prioritisation comparisons, release planning and rich release notes, with migrations 0063 to 0085 (0067 to 0069 are unused numbers). Hosted mail delivery, hosted Cron, live Canny/UserVoice/Zendesk providers and whole-product acceptance remain separately unproven; see HANDOVER.md and ACCEPTANCE.md. Product screenshot: public/brand/releases/penny-0.1.1-1440.png

OPS-001.summary: The full five-role system ships: current operators share product access, Owners and Admins change workspace clock settings (OPS-008), and other configuration stays owner-only.
OPS-001.was: Every operator holds one role. **Owner**: everything, including installation configuration, ownership handover (OPS-002), integrations, export and erasure. **Admin**: all product work plus settings (including branding, INT-007, and sender identity, NOTIFY-013), boards, integrations, automation rules and the roles below Owner. **Product manager**: all product work on evidence, requests, moderation (including editing and removing published content, REQ-038), decisions, roadmap and releases. **Contributor**: the seat for support, sales and success staff, who capture evidence, record proxy votes (CAP-014), comment internally and read product records, but cannot moderate, publish, commit, change settings or see commercial fields unless granted (ROLE-001). **Viewer**: read-only. Contributor and Viewer seats are unlimited. Each role is checked in the business transaction like current authority, and a role change applies to the next request. Operators invited before roles ship become Product managers, which is today's behaviour: every operator equal, with owner-only configuration. *Policy: `operator.roles.v1`; default: the five roles above.* *Acceptance:* A base and browser journey signs in one operator per role and attempts every guarded action through its route and its UI: a Viewer is refused every write with 403; a Contributor captures evidence, records a proxy vote and comments internally but is refused moderation, publication, commitment, settings and every commercial field; a Product manager is refused settings, integrations and roles; an Admin is refused ownership handover, export and erasure; each refusal changes nothing; a role change takes effect on the operator's next request.

Contributor and Viewer seats are unlimited. Each role is checked in the business transaction like current authority, and a role change applies to the next request. Operators invited before the full roles system ships become Product managers. Current operators share product access; workspace clock settings admit Owners and Admins (OPS-008), while other configuration remains owner-only. *Policy: `operator.roles.v1`; default: the five roles above.* *Acceptance:* A base and browser journey signs in one operator per role and attempts every guarded action through its route and its UI: a Viewer is refused every write with 403; a Contributor captures evidence, records a proxy vote and comments internally but is refused moderation, publication, commitment, settings and every commercial field; a Product manager is refused settings, integrations and roles; an Admin is refused ownership handover, export and erasure; each refusal changes nothing; a role change takes effect on the operator's next request.

OPS-005.summary: After rer setup, local rer dev opens signed in as the owner and returns them to /setup until it is finished; local development has no outbox and silently suppresses mail.
OPS-005.was: The signed-in owner whose setup is unfinished completes it at `/setup`, and every `/app` document and client-side app navigation sends that owner there first. Finishing it opens the app, and later visits to `/setup` go to the app. A signed-out visitor to `/setup` is sent to sign-in and back, and a signed-in operator who is not the owner is never sent there. Setup completion is installation state recorded once by the owner under the same-origin and authority checks of the business transaction; it is not portable domain data and does not transfer in an archive. An installation that already has an active owner is treated as finished. `rer setup` and the local outbox sign-in return the owner to `/setup` until it is finished. Setup cannot finish until the owner has chosen the workspace timezone and seen the requester quiet hours (OPS-008) and entered the company name (INT-007) and the business postal address (NOTIFY-013).

An installation that already has an active owner is treated as finished. Setup cannot finish until the owner has chosen the workspace timezone and seen the requester quiet hours (OPS-008) and entered the company name (INT-007) and the business postal address (NOTIFY-013).

REQ-017.summary: Decline and its reversal ship on the operator request page, and a repeated decline with another reason keeps the earlier direct or mapped status for reversal.
REQ-017.was: An operator can decline a published request. A decline without a public reason is rejected. Declining sets the public status to Declined, adds the reason to the request history as a status update (REQ-015), and refuses new votes and requester comments while leaving existing ones visible and counted. Reversing a decline restores the request's previous public status.
REQ-017.now: An operator can decline a published request. A decline without a public reason is rejected. Declining sets the public status to Declined, adds the reason to the request history as a status update (REQ-015), and refuses new votes and requester comments while leaving existing ones visible and counted. Reversing a decline restores the request's previous public status. Decline and reversal ship through the operator request controls; repeating a decline with another reason preserves the prior direct or mapped status for reversal. *Acceptance:* Route tests and the 1440/390 customer and operator journeys in `tests/base/request-status-workflow.test.ts` and `tests/browser/request-decline.mjs` prove the required public reason, Declined status and history, refusal of new votes and comments, retention of existing votes and discussion, and restoration after repeated decline.

REQ-022.summary: Blocking and unblocking requesters ships in the private requester directory: a blocked person's participation is refused, their public content hidden and votes excluded, and unblocking restores all of it.
REQ-022.was: An operator can block a requester identity. A blocked identity's submissions, votes, comments, follows, and outcome responses are refused with 403; their published requests and comments are hidden from the portal but kept for operators; and their votes stop counting toward totals. Unblocking restores all of it.
REQ-022.now: An operator can block a requester identity. A blocked identity's submissions, votes, comments, follows, and outcome responses are refused with 403; their published requests and comments are hidden from the portal but kept for operators; and their votes stop counting toward totals. Unblocking restores all of it. Block and unblock ship in the private requester directory, and the server checks existing sessions on each participation write. *Acceptance:* `tests/base/requester-blocking.test.ts` and the 1440/390 journey in `tests/browser/requester-blocking.mjs` prove submission, vote, comment, follow and outcome refusal, public hiding and vote-count exclusion with operator records retained, and restored visibility, counts and participation after unblock. Refusing the audit write rolls back the block or unblock.

API-001.summary: Adds the votes:write scope for proxy-vote customer lookup and recording; the other eight scopes cover their resources' reads and writes.
API-001.was: A current native operator may issue a named optional-expiry REST key. Its random value is revealed once; only its hash persists. Route-selected scopes admit only documented requests, comments, status and release operations. Bearers never grant operator HTML, generated-function, export or owner configuration authority.
API-001.now: A current native operator may issue a named optional-expiry REST key. Its random value is revealed once; only its hash persists. Route-selected scopes are `requests:read`, `requests:write`, `comments:read`, `comments:write`, `status:read`, `status:write`, `releases:read`, `releases:write` and `votes:write`. The first eight admit their documented resource reads and writes; `votes:write` authorizes customer lookup at `GET /api/v1/proxy-vote-contacts` and recording an attributed customer proxy vote at `POST /api/v1/requests/:slug/proxy-votes`, without verification or email permission. Bearers never grant operator HTML, generated-function, export or owner configuration authority. *Acceptance:* A current token with `votes:write` records a proxy vote; a token without that scope is refused the same vote write and changes no vote or permission record; revocation refuses the next write.

INT-007.summary: Company name is collected at setup and used for sender identity; portal-wide branding, uploaded logos and favicons, credit-link selection and Admin branding controls remain unproved.

The logo and favicon are stored in the installation's R2 and served from its own origin at stable versioned paths, so no portal, widget or email view makes a third-party request for them. The brand reaches every customer-facing surface: the portal header (logo and name, linking to the company website when set, else to the board), the browser tab's icon and title on every portal page, the widget launcher and panel (WIDGET-001, WIDGET-003), the changelog page and feeds (REL-015, REL-016), the SSO sign-in page (WIDGET-008), and every requester and release email (NOTIFY-001, REL-005), whose header carries the logo and company name and whose sender name follows NOTIFY-013. A change applies to the next page load and the next message composed. Without a logo the header shows the name alone and the tab shows a neutral default icon, never a customer's. A non-image file, a file over the limit and an SVG that fails sanitising are refused before storage; a Product manager, Contributor or Viewer is refused every branding write with 403. Branding (name, files, colours, theme, link) participates in product archives (DATA-001). Hosted hostname and egress provisioning require their actual authorized deployment paths. OPS-008.summary: Owners and Admins set the workspace timezone and requester quiet hours in Admin settings, effective from the change for clocks, SLAs and queued requester sends.
OPS-008.was: First-run setup (OPS-005) asks the owner for the workspace timezone, an IANA timezone pre-selected from the owner's browser (or from the `WORKSPACE_TIMEZONE` deployment input when it is set), and refuses Finish without one. The choice is stored as installation state that Owners and Admins change later in settings; once stored it is the `workspaceTimezone` every clause uses (NOTIFY-002, DEC-007, REL-014), and no installation that has recorded a choice falls back to a built-in default. An installation that finished setup before this ships shows its owner a one-time prompt, on their next sign-in, to confirm or change the current timezone. Settings also hold the requester quiet hours, shown beside the timezone at setup: off, or a start and an end hour in the workspace timezone (default 20:00 to 08:00). Operator email never has quiet hours (NOTIFY-003). A change applies at the next send check, and turning quiet hours off makes every held requester message due at once. The `WORKSPACE_TIMEZONE` input and the fixed 20:00–08:00 hours ship today; setup asks for no timezone and the hours cannot be changed. *Acceptance:* A base and browser journey: setup refuses Finish without a timezone; setup under an `America/New_York` browser timezone stores `America/New_York`; with the default quiet hours, a status update published at 21:00 Eastern sends at 08:00 Eastern and one published at 14:00 Eastern sends within NOTIFY-002's coalescing window; with quiet hours off, an update published at 23:00 Eastern sends within the coalescing window; changing the timezone in settings moves the next quiet period; the confirmation prompt appears once for an installation set up before the change.

Changes take effect for clocks and SLAs from the change, including the next queued requester send check and calendar-based decision review check. *Acceptance:* A base and browser journey: setup refuses Finish without a timezone; setup under an `America/New_York` browser timezone stores `America/New_York`; with the default quiet hours, a status update published at 21:00 Eastern sends at 08:00 Eastern and one published at 14:00 Eastern sends within NOTIFY-002's coalescing window; with quiet hours off, an update published at 23:00 Eastern sends within the coalescing window; changing the timezone in settings moves the next quiet period; the confirmation prompt appears once for an installation set up before the change; an Owner and an Admin each save the timezone and quiet-hours schedule in Admin, an ordinary operator is refused with 403, and changing the timezone changes a calendar review's next due check while turning quiet hours off releases queued requester mail without delaying operator mail.

CAP-014.summary: Native proxy votes are recorded from the inbox, the request page and a private Zendesk sidebar (proved with a network-edge fixture), and UserVoice imports keep their historical proxy marks.
CAP-014.was: An operator records a vote on behalf of a customer (an existing requester, a connector contact, or a new unverified contact) with the source that justifies it. A proxy vote counts once per customer in demand (REQ-026, SEG-007), is marked proxy with who recorded it, collapses with that customer's own later vote, grants no verified identity or email consent (REQ-010), and appears publicly only inside the vote total. Today the proxy mark exists only for supporters imported from UserVoice (IMP-008). *Acceptance:* A base test records proxy votes from the inbox and from a Zendesk sidebar fixture: each counts once, collapses with the customer's own later vote, creates no permission record, and appears in the CSV export with its recorder.

A proxy vote counts once per customer in demand (REQ-026, SEG-007), is marked proxy with who recorded it, collapses with that customer's own later vote, grants no verified identity or email consent (REQ-010), and appears publicly only inside the vote total. Native proxy recording ships from the inbox, the request page and the private Zendesk sidebar at the connector edge; supporters imported from UserVoice (IMP-008) also retain their historical proxy marks. The Zendesk SDK/proxy is proved with a network-edge fixture; a live Zendesk installation is not claimed. *Acceptance:* A base test records proxy votes from the inbox, the request page and a Zendesk sidebar fixture: each counts once, collapses with the customer's own later vote, creates no permission record, and appears in the CSV export with its recorder.

REQ-036.summary: All six direct public statuses, status comments, per-status templates, public month or quarter ETAs and unchanged-save deduplication ship.
REQ-036.was: On any published request an operator changes the status in one action, as Canny's status picker does: one of REQ-016's six public statuses directly, or an internal status (PRIO-002), which sets its mapped public status. The change takes an optional public comment, prefilled from the owner's template for that public status (one per status in settings, editable per change, blank by default), and an optional public ETA of a month or a quarter, which the request shows and the status roadmap (ROAD-014) shows beside it and which can be changed or cleared. Saving publishes one status update (REQ-015) carrying the new status and any comment into the request history, and the public status follows within 5 seconds under REQ-016. It notifies once per change each follower, vote-subscribed voter (NOTIFY-008) and subscribed author (NOTIFY-011) under NOTIFY-001 and NOTIFY-002, and NOTIFY-009's captured contacts when ticked; a change with no comment still sends a status-change message naming the new status. Declined still requires a public reason (REQ-017). Saving the same status again with no comment and no ETA change publishes and sends nothing. A bulk status change (TRIAGE-005) sends one message per request and recipient, coalesced under NOTIFY-002. The request ETA is set by the operator and never derived from an internal target date (ROAD-012). Today the operator request page publishes a status update that sets Open, Under review or Declined with required wording; Planned, In progress and Shipped, internal statuses, the optional comment, templates and the request ETA are missing. *Acceptance:* A base and browser journey: setting Planned with no comment on a published request that has no roadmap item shows Planned in every public payload within 5 seconds and emails each vote-subscribed voter and follower once; the request appears in the status roadmap's Planned column with its ETA; an internal status mapped to In progress shows In progress publicly and its own name only to operators; the template prefills and the published comment is the edited wording; saving the same status again sends nothing; Declined without a reason is refused.

NOTIFY-008.summary: A supporter recorded through CAP-014's native proxy controls on a vote-subscription board gets no permission record and no status-update email unless independently subscribed.
NOTIFY-008.was: Owners and Admins turn on, per board in settings, "Voting subscribes to updates", which is how Canny closes the loop with voters. On such a board the vote control tells the voter, before they vote, that voting subscribes them to updates on that request and how to stop; the vote then follows the request (REQ-010) and stores a timestamped permission record with its origin (vote), board and setting version, so status updates (REQ-015, ROAD-008), decline (REQ-017) and the release that ships it (REL-004) reach that voter under NOTIFY-001 and NOTIFY-002. Every such email says why it was sent ("You voted for …") and carries the one-click unsubscribe (NOTIFY-002), which withdraws the permission, and the owner's postal address (NOTIFY-013, CAN-SPAM); the setting cannot be turned on until that address is recorded. Removing the vote withdraws a vote-origin permission unless the voter also followed or ticked "Email me updates". Turning the setting off stops new vote subscriptions and keeps existing ones; the owner may also withdraw every vote-origin permission on that board, with a recorded reason. Proxy votes (CAP-014) and historical imported votes never subscribe (MIG-007 is the only import path). The author's subscription on submission is NOTIFY-011. New boards default to on; boards that exist when this ships keep it off until the owner chooses. *Acceptance:* A base and browser journey: with the setting on, the vote control states the subscription, and a vote creates one permission record with origin vote; a published status update emails that voter once; the email's unsubscribe link withdraws the permission and the next update sends nothing; removing a vote withdraws its permission while a voter who also followed keeps theirs; with the setting off a vote creates no record; a proxy vote creates no record.
